text: Paradoxical though it may seem, the passage through consciousness or self moves contrary to self, rubs it the wrong way - and in the end, will even rub it out.
note: Confirmed verbatim on the Awakening to Reality and spiritualteachers.org reposts.

text: As I see it, without a personal God, the Buddhist must have a much stronger faith in the "unconditioned and unbegotten".
note: Full sentence of catalogue fragment q0608ea9b; confirmed on four reposts.

text: "personal God" is any subjective experience of the divine.
note: From the same answer: consciousness is the human faculty for experiencing the divine.

text: Without a personal, subjective self, we could not even speak of an impersonal, non-subjective God; one is just relative to the other.
If we tried to do so, we would either end up with another side, or the whole coin would collapse, leaving no center at all.
note: Sentence adjacent to the 'divine center - the coin' passage (q147cc879); the antecedent of 'to do so' (separating the two sides of the coin) is not in the snippet.

text: No-self, then, means no-consciousness.
note: Complete sentence; preceded by 'the terms "self" and "consciousness" express the same experiences' (q32025793).

text: the storms, crises and sufferings of life are a way of finding the eye
note: Companion line of the stillpoint/cyclone passage; quote sites vary the exact text.

text: Christ articulated the eye in more positive terms as the "Kingdom of God" or the "Spirit within"
note: Stillpoint passage; also tagged by Goodreads to The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path.

text: Buddha's "emptiness" or "void", a refuge from the swirling cyclone of endless suffering
note: Corrects catalogue qbbc255fb ('endless suffering').

text: authors come up with various stages, depending on the criteria they are using
note: From the stage-theory answer (Teresa's seven mansions given as an example).

text: it is always someone else's retrospective view of his or her own journey, which may not include our own experiences or insights
note: Same answer as 'I don't think we should get locked into any stage theory'.

text: our obligation is to be true to our own insights, our own inner light
note: Search summary: 'This phrase appears in several reprints of the interview.'

text: the terms "purgative", "illuminative", and "unitive" (often used of the contemplative path) do not refer to discrete stages, but to a way of travel
note: Opening of her answer to the first question (the first three stages of the Christian contemplative life).

text: once we come to the state of oneness, we can go no further with the inward journey
note: Continues (paraphrase) that the movement then turns outward: 'the center is expanding outward'.

text: Could you talk briefly about the first three stages of the Christian contemplative life as you experienced them
note: NOT her words: Stephan Bodian's opening question (recorded for context).

text: But I must preface this account by saying that on previous occasions, I had come upon a pervasive silence of the faculties so total as to give rise to subtle apprehensions of fear.
note: Primary excerpt (Perlego). Replaces the blogger paraphrase in q64642b84.

text: Because this was the limit of my expectations, I was all the more surprised and bewildered when many years later I came upon a permanent state in which there was no self
note: Second sentence of the Introduction, following 'Within the traditional framework...'.

text: This journey then, is nothing more, yet nothing less than a period of acclimating to a new way of seeing, a time of transition and revelation as it gradually comes upon "that" which remains when there is no self. This is not a journey for those who expect love and bliss.
note: Full passage behind catalogue fragment q38827d6b; aggregator host (minimalistquotes) with capitalisation normalised.

text: no-self is not God; rather, it is the gap between self and God
note: Reported in a search summary of the epdf.pub full-text copy as her statement; exact wording not seen.

text: As the river flows, from out of the formless void arises the greatest of great realities, a simple smile.
note: Quotation page surfaced in the 'absolute nothingness' search; innerexplorations gives the shorter 'out of nothingness arises the greatest of great realities' and p.81 for 'absolute nothingness'. Host of the longer line uncertain (Western Mystics page likely).

text: It can no longer be tested by any force or trial, nor moved by the winds of change, and at this point the self has obviously outworn its function; it is no longer needed or useful, and life can go on without it.
note: Full sentence behind catalogue fragments qa2082e12 and q03c1375a; aggregators cite p.5. Variant 'outgrown' on goldenageofgaia.

text: The path to no-self, then, is the egoless unitive state.
note: Preface sentence surfaced from the pdfcoffee full-text copy.

text: From the unitive state outward to the end of the marketplace stage, however, is the unknown path to no-self, a stage not often recognized in contemplative literature.
where no such account exists, we assume there is no path and that union of self and God is the final goal to be achieved
note: Precedes 'The assumption that the egoless condition ... is a great mistake.'

text: what the final stage really is, or how far God will stretch man's original design, no one knows
the unitive state follows the falling away or transcendence of the ego and entails a radical change or transformation of consciousness
note: Continuation of the book's opening sentence (qf3f06c8c).

text: It may be the end of the ego-self, but by no means is it the end of the self—either the true self or the phenomenal self.
the unitive state is no longer regarded as the ultimate goal but, instead, is seen as the midpoint of the passage
Since God is neither mother, father, son or daughter, these metaphors must not be taken literally or understood as God ad intra (God-in-Itself).
note: Full sentence of catalogue fragment qa88289be; on the archive.org text and the Bernadette's Friends blog.

text: this book refers to God's Triune essence as "Transcendent-Logos-Spirit"
note: Immediately follows the 'God ad intra' sentence ('to avoid that pitfall').

text: Christ is not the oneness of two persons, two individuals or two beings (a divine being and a human being), rather, Christ is the eternal oneness of two natures, divine and human.
note: Full sentence behind q196b5e82 and q743f2e6e.

text: if the incarnation was just about one human being's oneness with God, it would be meaningless to the rest of mankind
Christ is God creating Its own human nature - i.e., man's one universal human nature - eternally one with Itself
note: On the students' blog summary of the book.

text: the name "Jesus" is solely a reference to a particular human being or person
his human nature was totally changed, transfigured and glorified
note: On Jesus' humanity after the resurrection.

text: Of first importance is to define the major terms used in this book, namely "Logos", "Christ", and "Jesus". Those who think these terms are interchangeable...
note: Truncated in the blog snippet; continues that treating the terms as interchangeable will obscure the argument.

text: God is not a being, but Infinite Existence, so we must avoid treating the Trinity as three beings
note: Search-summary rendering of a blog passage; wording not verbatim.

text: Truly, God is all that exists–all, of course, but the self.
book: autobiographical sketch: Mystics, Masters, Saints and Sages (2001)
note: Closing line of her self-written sketch in Ullman & Reichenberg-Ullman, 'Mystics, Masters, Saints and Sages'; the source of St. Romain's 'God is everything that exists ... except the self' (q336b7ef3).

text: that which acts, that which it acts upon, and the act itself are one without division
book: How it Works (short essay reproduced on Western Mystics)
note: Adjacent to 'It never goes outside itself to know itself...' (qdde04e58).

text: there is no multiplicity of existences; only what Is has existence, an existence that can expand itself into an infinite variety of forms
book: How it Works (short essay reproduced on Western Mystics)

text: grace does not favor anyone on the basis of genes, family, or culture
book: Contemplative: Autobiography of the Early Years
note: Search-summary rendering of the preface passage that follows the genes-and-environment sentence (qf08dbd7b).

text: Where Buddha described the experience, Christ manifested it without words; yet they both make the same statement and reveal the same truth: that ultimately, eternal life is beyond self or consciousness.
book: Essays on the Christian Contemplative Journey
note: Full sentence behind catalogue qc5b19862 (which stops at 'same truth'). Goodreads only.
